rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 89, Line 1, Exception: "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "2. You received a refund other than an income tax refund, such as a general sales tax or real property tax refund, in 2025 of an amount deducted or credit claimed in an earlier year" and "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025". Exceptions 1 and 5 are refused by refund.not_2024 ("Is any of these refunds for a tax year other than 2024 (box 3 of Form 1099-G), or did you pay any of your 2024 state or local income tax in 2025?", reworded under BUG-0230 and now wider than exception 5), whose refusal sits on refund.taxable, the line Schedule 1 line 1 enters, so no such refund reaches line 1 on a completed return; the model saw only line 1's two refusals (exc_tax, exc_who: items 3, 4, 6 to 9). Exception 2 is outside refund.received ("State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets") and refused by scope.schedule1 ("a refund or other recovery of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year, other than a state or local income tax refund (for example a refund of general sales tax, real estate tax or personal property tax ...)"): refusal located on the reading line. The smaller of refund.received and 2024 Schedule A line 5d matches the worksheet (amb.2025.refund_cap_5d (owner decision D6(a), Stage 16: cap line 1 at 2024 Schedule A line 5d as printed; a refund above the income tax part is exception 4 territory, refund.exc_tax)). Same as the archived ruling, rechecked against the reworded screen. Project retained.

rulings.model: IRS line 6 says 'Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)' and for MFS permits spouse boxes only if the spouse had no income, isn't filing, and can't be claimed; the restatement just adds box amounts and omits the MFS spouse eligibility condition.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" and footnote "*If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn’t filing a return, and can’t be claimed as a dependent on another person’s return"; p. 33, Line 12d: "Don’t check any boxes for your spouse if your filing status is head of household". The married filing separately condition is in the spouse questions themselves (refund.spouse_born, refund.spouse_blind: "If your 2024 filing status was married filing separately, answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return"), as the footnote says; amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 records the status reading; the restatement's status condition zeroes the spouse boxes for single, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse, and the footnote's further conditions for a separate return are answered in the questions, not in the expression. Each per-box helper is refund.per_box when its box is checked and zero otherwise, and refund.per_box is labelled and encoded "$1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" (single/hoh -> refund.box_unmarried $1,950; mfj/mfs/qss -> refund.box_married $1,550), so the sum is the number of boxes times the amount. Same as the archived ruling. Project retained. rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)". Each per-box helper is refund.per_box ("$1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)": single/hoh -> refund.box_unmarried $1,950; mfj/mfs/qss -> refund.box_married $1,550) when its box is checked and zero otherwise, so the sum is boxes times the rate. The MFS footnote ("If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return") is carried in the spouse questions refund.spouse_born and refund.spouse_blind ("If your 2024 filing status was married filing separately, answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent"). The model's "adds per-box amounts" is the same quantity as the count times the rate. On the qualifying-surviving-spouse point (spouse boxes zero unless 2024 status MFJ or MFS): ambiguity, amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 (chosen reading: "ask the spouse questions only when the 2024 filing status was married filing jointly or married filing separately"); the worksheet is silent on QSS, and on the 2024 Form 1040 the spouse boxes belong to a spouse on the return.
